entries.name: Japan Address Lookup (Postal Code)
entries.description: Look up Japanese address candidates for a 7-digit Japanese postal code (郵便番号), backed by the official Japan Post KEN_ALL dataset. One postal code can map to several towns; all candidates are returned with kanji and kana readings. Useful for Japanese address autofill and postal-code validation.

usage.callShape: GET https://address.agentic-jp.com/postal-code/{zip} — embed the 7-digit Japanese postal code directly in the URL path. No hyphen, no query params, no body. Pays $0.001 USDC via x402 on Base.
usage.outputShape: postal_code (string, hyphenated e.g. '100-0001'), candidates[] each with: candidates[].prefecture, candidates[].city, candidates[].town, candidates[].prefecture_kana, candidates[].city_kana, candidates[].town_kana
quirks: Input is the 7-digit postal code embedded in the URL path WITHOUT a hyphen (e.g. 1000001, not 100-0001). The response echoes it back hyphenated.
Japanese postal codes ONLY — does not validate US or international addresses.
Response field values (prefecture/city/town) are in Japanese kanji; kana readings are provided in *_kana fields. No English/romaji is returned.
Returns multiple candidates[] when one postal code maps to several towns.
The agentic-jp origin also exposes a POST /normalize endpoint (separate op, not part of this service).
qa-pay.mjs does not complete the x402 GET flow for this origin (returns 402 empty body, paid:false); verified instead via agentcash fetch which paid $0.001 and returned 200.

entries.name: Email Deliverability Verifier (Hunter)
entries.description: Verify the deliverability and validity of an email address via Hunter (proxied through StableEnrich). Returns a status classification plus a confidence score and granular signals (MX records, SMTP check, disposable/webmail/accept-all flags). NOT an address validator despite the original bundling.

usage.callShape: POST https://stableenrich.dev/api/hunter/email-verifier with JSON body {"email":"..."}. Pays $0.03 USDC via x402 (or mpp) on Base.
usage.outputShape: status (enum: valid|invalid|accept_all|webmail|disposable|unknown), score (number), email (string), regexp (bool), gibberish (bool), disposable (bool), webmail (bool), mx_records (bool), smtp_server (bool), smtp_check (bool), accept_all (bool), block (bool), sources[] (each: domain,uri,extracted_on,last_seen_on,still_on_page). ALTERNATIVELY a pending/async response: {jobId, status:'pending', pollUrl, retryAfterSeconds}
quirks: This backend is an EMAIL verifier, not an address validator — it was misclassified under 'Address Validator'.
Single required field 'email' in the JSON body.

Fast/cached verifications return the final result immediately (200). Hunter-pending responses instead return {jobId, status:'pending', pollUrl, retryAfterSeconds} which must be polled with SIWX at pollUrl.
Common public/disposable addresses come back status:'disposable' with score:0 (as seen for hello@example.com).

entries.name: Email Validator
entries.description: Validate a single email address: syntax/RFC check, MX record lookup, disposable-domain detection (5,000+ domains), free-provider and role-based flags, and a typo suggestion (did_you_mean) — returns a trust score and deliverability status without ever sending mail. Use to qualify leads, clean lists, and gate signups.

inputSchema.email: string (required) — email address to validate, passed as ?email= query param
string (required) — email address to verify (max 254 chars), passed as ?email= query param
string (required) — email address to check, passed as ?email= query param
inputSchema.checkMx: boolean (optional, default true) — look up MX-record presence via DNS-over-HTTPS; set false to skip the DNS lookup

data.items: array of { email:string, normalized:string, local:string, domain:string, isSyntaxValid:boolean, isDisposable:boolean, isRoleAccount:boolean, isFreeProvider:boolean, hasMxRecords:boolean, mxHosts:string[], reason:string|null, note:string, source:object }

outputSchema.meta: object { endpoint:string, version:string|null, caller:string, cost:{usd:number}, settlement:{txHash:string, network:string, success:boolean} }

usage.callShape: DEFAULT (mailcheck): POST https://mailcheck.hugen.tokyo/mailcheck/validate with JSON body {"email":"<address>"}. Synchronous JSON, no polling. x402node alternative is GET https://api.x402node.dev/validate/email?email=<address> (no body). Pay via x402 USDC on Base.
usage.outputShape: DEFAULT (mailcheck): body.status ('valid'|...), body.score (0..1), body.syntax_valid, body.domain, body.mx_found, body.mx_records[], body.is_disposable, body.is_free, body.is_role_based, body.did_you_mean (non-null on likely typo), body.checks_performed[]
quirks: MULTI-GATEWAY: same operation across 3 providers but DIFFERENT call shapes — mailcheck is POST with a JSON body {"email":...}; netintel & x402node are GET with ?email= query param and NO body. Do not send a body to the GET backends.

Output field names DIFFER by backend and do not align: mailcheck uses is_free / mx_found / did_you_mean / status+score(0..1); x402node uses valid / format / mxValid; netintel uses is_free_provider / mx_records_found / deliverability / score(0..100). Normalize per-backend, never assume a shared shape.

DEFAULT = mailcheck (richest + verified). Gate deliverability on body.status + body.score; body.is_disposable / body.is_role_based / body.mx_found give detail; body.did_you_mean is non-null when a typo is detected (e.g. gmial.com -> gmail.com).
netintel (netintel-production-440c.up.railway.app) is BROKEN: every paid request returns 402 {"error":"Settlement failed","details":"unknown_error"} — it never settles. Exclude it from routing.
mailcheck returned confirmed:false (no txHash echoed) but HTTP 200 with full body — settlement confirmation is async/not echoed; the response itself is the proof of success.
Synchronous JSON response on all working backends — no job id / no polling.
Not outward/irreversible: validation only reads DNS/MX, never sends email.

entries.name: Crypto Address Validator
entries.description: Validate cryptocurrency wallet addresses across chains and detect their network/format. Pay-per-call x402.

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/crypto/address-validate?chain={chain}&address={address} (required query params; chain enum: btc|eth|sol|ltc|trx|xrp|bch)
usage.outputShape: body.data.items[0].valid (boolean), body.data.items[0].canonical (normalized address), body.data.items[0].format (e.g. eip-55), body.data.items[0].reason (null if valid); body.data.ok and body.data.total summarize the batch
usage.guide: Call GET https://2s.io/api/crypto/address-validate with two required query params: chain (one of btc, eth, sol, ltc, trx, xrp, bch) and address (the wallet address string). Payment is x402 USDC ($0.001) on Base or Solana; no API key. Read the result from body.data.items[0]: valid tells you if the address is well-formed for that chain, canonical gives the normalized address, format names the encoding, and reason explains failures when valid is false.

entries.name: NetIntel Email Authentication
entries.description: Checks a sending domain's email authentication — validates SPF, DKIM (probing many selectors), and DMARC records, flags spoofing risks and misconfigurations, and returns an A-F email-security grade with transparent scored deductions.

domain.description: Sending domain to assess (e.g. example.org) — JSON body field. Bare domain, not an email address.

usage.callShape: POST https://netintel.dev/email-auth with JSON body {domain:'<domain>'} (bare sending domain, NOT an email address). x402 pay-per-call (USDC on Base eip155:8453 OR Solana), $0.002, no API key. First unpaid request returns 402 with the accepts array; retry the same request with an X-PAYMENT header.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON. Top level: domain, resolves (bool), grade (A-F), score (0-100). spf{found, record, mechanisms[], all_qualifier, dns_lookup_count, issues[]}. dkim{found, selectors_checked[] (~14 common selectors probed), records[]{selector, record, key_type, key_length_bits, issues[]}, issues[]}. dmarc{found, record, policy, subdomain_policy, pct, rua[], ruf[], issues[]}. deductions[]{rule, points, detail}. Verified live: {domain:'example.org', resolves:true, grade:'C', score:72, spf:{found:true, record:'v=spf1 -all', all_qualifier:'-all'}, dkim:{found:false, issue 'No DKIM record found for any selector' -20}, dmarc:{found:true, policy:'reject', subdomain_policy:'reject', pct:100, no rua -5, no ruf -3}, deductions:[dkim_none_found -20, dmarc_no_rua -5, dmarc_no_ruf -3]}.
quirks: Input is the DOMAIN as a JSON body field {domain:'...'} on a POST — a bare sending domain, NOT an email address (contrast /email-intel/analyze which takes an address, and /email-report/full which takes ?email= as a query param).
This host (netintel.dev) advertises TWO accepts: Base USDC (eip155:8453) AND Solana USDC — paid cleanly on Base at $0.002.

DKIM discovery is best-effort: it probes ~14 common selectors (default, google, selector1/2, k1/2, s1/2, dkim, mail, smtp, mandrill, everlytickey1, mxvault); a domain using a non-standard selector may show dkim.found=false even if DKIM exists — read dkim.records[] for what was actually seen.
Grade/score are driven by deductions[] ({rule, points, detail}); gate on grade + score for the headline, read spf/dkim/dmarc.issues[] and deductions[] for the detail.
NetIntel does not charge on 4xx/5xx (input-validation, upstream, or server errors) per its Agent Fair-Trade guarantee; SSRF-safe.
usage.guide: Check a sending domain's email authentication posture in one call: POST https://netintel.dev/email-auth with JSON body {domain:'<domain>'} (a bare domain such as example.org, NOT an email address). Pay via x402 (USDC on Base eip155:8453 or Solana, $0.002/call, no API key): the first unpaid request returns HTTP 402 with the accepts array; retry the same request with an X-PAYMENT header. The 200 response is synchronous, self-contained JSON — read grade (A-F) + score (0-100) for the headline, then spf{record, all_qualifier, issues[]}, dkim{found, selectors_checked[], records[], issues[]} (it probes ~14 common selectors), and dmarc{policy, subdomain_policy, pct, rua/ruf, issues[]}, plus deductions[] ({rule, points, detail}) for why the grade landed where it did. No polling. This is NetIntel's authentication-only slice — narrower than 'NetIntel Email Report' (which also folds in address intelligence + optional breach) and keyed on a domain rather than an address.

entries.name: NetIntel Email Report
entries.description: Fully vet an email address and its domain in one call — combines SPF/DKIM/DMARC authentication, deliverability and disposable/role/free-provider intelligence, and an optional password breach check into a single trust verdict with score, grade, and findings.

inputSchema.email: string (required) — email address to vet, passed as ?email= query param (e.g. user@example.com)
inputSchema.password: string (optional) — if supplied, the breach section runs a k-anonymity HIBP check and returns {breached, breach_count, risk_level}; omitted → breach section returns error:'not_requested' (full password never transmitted, only a SHA-1 prefix)

sections.authentication: { available: boolean, spf: string, dkim: string, dmarc: string }
sections.intelligence: { available: boolean, deliverability: string, is_disposable: boolean, is_role_based: boolean, is_free_provider: boolean }
sections.breach: { available: boolean, error?: string, breached?: boolean, breach_count?: number, risk_level?: string }

outputSchema.findings: array of { rule: string, deduction: number, detail: string }

usage.callShape: GET https://netintel.dev/email-report/full?email=<address> (optionally &password=<pw> to enable the breach section) — email passed as a query param; x402 pay-per-call (USDC on Base eip155:8453 or Solana), $0.15, no API key. First unpaid request returns 402 with accepts; retry the same request with an X-PAYMENT header.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON report: body.email, body.domain, body.generated_at (ISO). body.sections.authentication{available,spf,dkim,dmarc}, body.sections.intelligence{available,deliverability,is_disposable,is_role_based,is_free_provider}, body.sections.breach{available,error|breached,breach_count,risk_level}. Aggregate: body.sections_ok/body.sections_failed (counts), body.trust_verdict (e.g. 'trusted'|'untrusted'), body.score (0-100), body.grade (A-F), body.findings[] ({rule,deduction,detail}). Verified live: {email:'test@example.org', domain:'example.org', authentication:{spf:'pass',dkim:'missing',dmarc:'p=reject'}, intelligence:{deliverability:'undeliverable'}, breach:{available:false,error:'not_requested'}, trust_verdict:'untrusted', score:70, grade:'C', findings:[{rule:'undeliverable',deduction:-30}]}.
quirks: email is a QUERY PARAM on a GET (?email=...), not a JSON body.

The breach section is OPT-IN: omit password → breach.available=false, error='not_requested'; supply &password=<pw> → k-anonymity HaveIBeenPwned check ({breached,breach_count,risk_level}), full password never transmitted (only a SHA-1 prefix).

Composite report — a superset of the standalone /email-intel/analyze (validation) and /email-auth (domain auth) endpoints; each of the three sections runs concurrently with graceful partial-failure handling (sections_ok/sections_failed track how many succeeded), so a section can be available:false without failing the whole call.

Gate on body.trust_verdict + body.score/body.grade for the headline; read body.sections.* and body.findings[] for the detail (e.g. finding rule 'undeliverable' deducts -30 when the domain has no MX records).
Failed calls (4xx/5xx, incl. input-validation rejections) are never charged per NetIntel's Agent Fair-Trade Agreement; SSRF-safe (blocks private/internal targets).
usage.guide: Fully vet an email and its domain in one call: GET https://netintel.dev/email-report/full with the address in the ?email= query param (e.g. ?email=test@example.org). To also run a breach check on a candidate password, add &password=<pw> (k-anonymity HIBP — the full password is never sent). Pay via x402 (USDC on Base or Solana, $0.15/call, no API key): the first unpaid request returns HTTP 402 with the accepts array; retry the same request with an X-PAYMENT header. The 200 response is synchronous, self-contained JSON: read body.trust_verdict + body.score (0-100)/body.grade (A-F) for the headline, then body.sections.authentication (spf/dkim/dmarc), body.sections.intelligence (deliverability, is_disposable/is_role_based/is_free_provider), and body.sections.breach for the per-section detail, plus body.findings[] for the deductions. No polling. This is NetIntel's composite email-trust report — a superset of the 'Email Validator' (validation-only) capability.

entries.name: NetIntel Phone Intel
entries.description: Parse and validate any phone number offline — normalize it to E.164, international, and national formats, identify its country and line type (mobile/landline/VOIP/toll-free/premium for NANP + UK), catch fictional/unassigned numbers, and return a validity verdict with a trust score, grade, and findings, without a paid telecom API.

inputSchema.phone: string (required) — phone number in any format (e.g. '+1 555 867-5309'), passed as ?phone= query param; URL-encode a leading + as %2B
inputSchema.country_hint: string (optional) — ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code hint (e.g. 'US') when the number has no dial code

usage.callShape: GET https://netintel.dev/phone-intel/analyze?phone=<number> — phone passed as a query param (URL-encode a leading + as %2B); optional &country_hint=<ISO alpha-2>. x402 pay-per-call (USDC on Base eip155:8453 or Solana), $0.05, no API key. First unpaid request returns 402 with accepts; retry with X-PAYMENT.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous flat JSON: body.input (echo), body.is_valid (bool), body.e164/international/national (formatted strings), body.country_code (dial code), body.country (ISO alpha-2), body.country_name, body.line_type (mobile|landline|mobile_or_landline|voip|toll_free|premium|unknown; only resolved for NANP + UK, else 'unknown'), body.digit_count, body.score (0-100), body.grade (A-F), body.findings[] ({rule, deduction, detail} e.g. 'unassigned_area_code' for a 555 fictional number).
quirks: phone is a QUERY PARAM on a GET (?phone=...), not a JSON body. URL-encode a leading + as %2B — an unencoded + in a query string decodes to a space (a leading space+digits is tolerated and re-interpreted as +).

Offline numbering-plan parser (libphonenumber-style), NOT a live telecom/carrier query: line_type is resolved only for NANP + UK numbers (mobile/landline/VOIP/toll-free/premium); other countries return line_type 'unknown'. This is a different capability from the carrier-network lookups (BlockRun Twilio, StablePhone).

Catches fictional/unassigned NANP numbers (555 area code, 555-01XX range) — the documented example '+1 (555) 867-5309' returns is_valid:false, score:0, grade:'F' with a findings 'unassigned_area_code' entry, yet still a 200 with full parse/format output.
Gate validity on body.is_valid + body.score/body.grade; use body.e164 for storage/normalization and body.findings[] for the specific deductions.
Failed calls (4xx/5xx, incl. input-validation rejections) are never charged per NetIntel's Agent Fair-Trade Agreement; SSRF-safe (blocks private/internal targets).
usage.guide: Validate/parse a phone number by calling GET https://netintel.dev/phone-intel/analyze with the number in the ?phone= query param, e.g. ?phone=%2B1%20(555)%20867-5309 (URL-encode a leading + as %2B, or an unencoded + decodes to a space). Add &country_hint=US when the number has no dial code. Pay via x402 (USDC on Base or Solana, $0.05/call, no API key): the first unpaid request returns HTTP 402 with the accepts array; retry the same request with an X-PAYMENT header. The 200 response is synchronous, self-contained JSON: read body.is_valid plus body.score (0-100)/body.grade (A-F) for the verdict, body.e164/international/national for normalized formats, body.country_name + body.line_type for context, and body.findings[] for the deductions (e.g. fictional 555 numbers flag 'unassigned_area_code'). No polling. This is an offline numbering-plan parser (line_type resolved only for NANP + UK), distinct from live carrier/Twilio lookups.

entries.name: 24kLabs Email Validator
entries.description: Validate an email address with an RFC-5322-ish syntax check plus disposable / role-account / free-provider flags and the parsed domain.

result.role_account: boolean (flag: role account e.g. info@, admin@)

usage.outputShape: json: { service, result: { valid, domain, disposable, free_provider, role_account }, latency_ms } — result carries the boolean flags and parsed domain
usage.quirks: Single-shot synchronous validator; result is inline in the 200 (no polling). Syntax + heuristic flags only (no live SMTP/MX deliverability check). The /api/v1/email-validate path is the same op on the same host (a namespace alias) and must not be indexed/paid separately.
usage.guide: Send a POST with JSON { email }. Example: {"email":"user@example.com"} returns result.valid==true with domain, disposable, free_provider and role_account flags. Pays x402 (USDC on Base, $0.002/call); the result is inline in the 200 (no polling).
